Irene Morales: Launch note: weve opened a small MI250X warm/burst pool in Nairobi (NBO) for Hosted Dedicated customers. Goal: lower regional tail latency and provide short-term spike capacity.

Devon K: How big is the pool and what are tenant limits?

Irene Morales: 36 MI250X GPUs total. Per-tenant burst cap = 6 GPUs. Max single reservation = 6h, cooldown = 2h between reservations.

Nora Li: Is this visible in the console and billing immediately?

Irene Morales: Yes  it's visible in Console under "Capacity > Burst Pools" and billing shows a new line item labeled "burst-dedicated-mi250x-nbo". We apply a temporary 1.25x multiplier to Dedicated on-demand rates for burst usage.

Priya G: Any impact on Private/VPC customers?

Irene Morales: No impact. Private/VPC customers are not routed to this hosted warm pool. We will provide a separate advisory if/when theres a partner on-prem offering.

OpsBot: RUNBOOK: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mi250x-nbo-burst (includes alerts and escalation steps)

Devon K: Ops - what alerts should be watched?

Irene Morales: Key alerts: scheduler.queue.time > 1500ms for 5m, gpu.provision.error >= 3 in 10m, burst.pool.free < 10% for 15m. If triggered, page infra-backfill.

Nora Li: Any perf guidance for customers migrating models?

Irene Morales: Recommend small initial batches and limiting concurrency for first 5k tokens while KV caches warm. Optimized MI250X runtime build is scheduled for rollout tomorrow to reduce cold-start memory spikes.

Priya G: Docs and comms ownership?

Irene Morales: CS doing customer outreach; Product + Eng Docs own docs. Draft posted here: https://redwood.internal/docs/mi250x-nbo-preview. Please review.

Irene Morales: TL;DR: NBO MI250X warm pool live (36 GPUs), per-tenant cap 6, 6h max, canary with selected tenants started, self-serve reservations next week, temporary 1.25x pricing, runbook and CLI examples in docs. Ping me with questions. :rocket:

Devon K: Thanks all :thumbsup:
